steps.title: Count failed and unknown-account logins
steps.do: Type grep -c "Failed password" auth-jump01.log at the prompt while speaking, with no pause, then press Return. Rest the cursor on the 53 in the output. Type grep -c "invalid user" auth-jump01.log on the next prompt while speaking, with no pause, then press Return. Slide the cursor down onto the 14. Move the cursor between the 53 and the 14 and say they are the bar: the pivot has to say 53, or the import gets rechecked.
steps.type:
grep -c "Failed password" auth-jump01.log
grep -c "invalid user" auth-jump01.log
say: "Step 3: the failures. Typing, down at the prompt, grep dash c, Failed password in quotes, the log name, then Return, for a number to hit."
"It says 53, so that's 53 Failed password lines to match."
"Then below that, typing the same grep dash c but with invalid user in quotes, and Return, to count accounts that don't exist."
"14 invalid user lines, so someone's guessing usernames, not just fumbling a password."
"So both counts are my bar: if the pivot isn't 53, the import's wrong, and I'd recheck."

steps.title: Last look at the pivot and epilogue
steps.do: The pivot is still on screen. Slide the cursor down column A, then across to column E: six addresses ranked, a decision beside each. Run the cursor down E3 to E8: two Block, two Watch, two Ignore, six cells for the six pivot rows. Then read the closing paragraph as one single block, moving the cursor on the pivot as the spoken words reach each figure: D9, the 53; Sheet1 and Pivot Table 1 in the tab strip; the Data menu; the pivot header row; column A; column E; D4, the 14; D3, the 18; E5 and E6; D5 and D6; E7 and E8; D7, the 3; C7; D8, the 2; the whole table from A3 to E8; the File menu; then E3 to E8 again for Block 2, Watch 2, Ignore 2. At the end slide left off the grid and rest on the Dock at the left edge until the paragraph ends.
say: "Step 23: the pivot's still on screen, so that's the final look. Column A has the six addresses ranked, with a decision beside each in column E."
"E3 to E8 hold two Block, two Watch and two Ignore, six cells for the six pivot rows, so the counts match."

"So, start to finish. I began in Terminal and counted the log: 59 lines, 53 of them Failed password, and 14 of those on accounts that don't exist, so I had numbers to check against later. Then I brought the log export into Sheets and checked all 59 rows had come across. I froze the header, added a filter from the Data menu, and built a pivot of source address against event type, and its failure total came to 53, the same as Terminal, so I trusted it. After that I went down the ranking one address at a time, filtered to its rows, read the users and times, and typed a verdict beside it. The Block pair is the two biggest piles, 18 failures and 14, both from outside, with no login at all, and one of them only ever tried accounts that don't exist. That fits my rule: an outside address with five or more failures and no login gets blocked for 24 hours. The Watch pair failed 9 times and 7 times and then got in, one as svc_backup and one as jsmith. I didn't block them, because a block could lock out a real person, and a guessed password could still be live. So they get an account action instead: a password reset for svc_backup, and a check with jsmith. The Ignore pair is the internal admin, who mistyped three times and then logged in, with publickey logins either side, and one outside address with just 2 tries, under five and no login, which is noise. Neither of those needs a block. I copied the table into the note, wrote the action lines for the firewall owner, and downloaded the note and the sheet. So, for the goal: before the morning standup, last night's failed logins on jump01 are sorted. Block 2, Watch 2, Ignore 2, and the note tells the firewall owner what to act on, what to watch, and what to leave alone."
